svg.text: One floating ring. Six fixed half rings. The lake supplies the lower halves; together they weave one eye.
Six ribs and six reflections cross into one woven eye.
A FEW STEPS ALONG / THE CROSSINGS SLIDE
Low ribs pass under tall ones. Nothing touches.
ribs span about 6.5 to 6.7 m and rise 1.0 to 1.85 m; ring about 7 m
The eye is seen from the bottom of this panel.
Three tall one way, three low the other. Nine crossings.
Then a band of the chosen tone crosses its ring through the hour.
The conditions we shape: the basin walls, the ring and the six ribs.
What happens by itself: wake, weather, daylight, and twenty weeks of fouling.
Each rib with its reflected half, and the light that threads through them.
The mother: here a floating ring and the round of lake it holds.
A bubble in kitchen foam is a few millimetres across. The widest rib is more than a thousand times that.
Illustrative optical-study geometry. Not a site survey, mooring plan, navigation plan or engineered design. Reflections are virtual; nothing below the waterline is built.
